lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Owned the claims backlog report and the weekly numbers the claims managers used.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Wrote the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Improved reporting efficiency by 90% by moving the monthly revenue report to scheduled SQL queries.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.
- Wrote data-quality checks on the 40 most-used tables, catching 15 broken loads before they reached a dashboard.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Reported the national conversion rate as the simple average of 14 regional conversion rates, without weighting by regional traffic.
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Compared the forecast with the operator's rebalancing schedule: empty-station hours fell from 310 to 205 a week in a replay of last summer.
- Published the notebooks and a short write-up, which the city's open-data team linked from its bike-share page.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Built a retention dashboard for about 2.4 million shoppers that raised repeat purchases by nearly a quarter.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the profile link is working and complete in the submitted résumé.
items.because: The supplied address appears anonymized.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requires them.
items.because: They are not needed to assess analytics qualifications, and nationality is not the same as work authorization.

items.says: Consider shortening the education entry.
items.because: That could make room for more relevant experience.

items.says: Clarify your responsibility for the claims reporting and how managers used it.
items.because: “The weekly numbers” is vague and does not show the report’s purpose or scope.

items.says: Clarify whether you recommended or implemented the staffing change and verify its connection to the hold-time reduction.
items.because: The attribution needs to be defensible.

items.says: Explain how the before-and-after hold-time periods were measured.
items.because: The review asks for a defensible basis for the result.

items.says: Give a timeframe and comparison basis for the claim that query errors fell by half.
items.because: Without that context, the size of the improvement is hard to interpret.

items.says: Separate the fraud-flag automation from the unrelated duties or remove the less relevant duties.
items.because: Bundling them obscures the technical contribution and its connection to the time saving.

items.says: Verify how the 10-hours-a-month saving was estimated.
items.because: The current bullet makes that saving hard to connect to the automation.

items.says: Define what the 90% reporting-efficiency improvement measures and how it was calculated.
items.because: As written, the large claim is ambiguous.

items.says: The stated SQL method does not reliably find customers with no orders.
items.because: It must preserve customer records and check for a missing value on the orders side; a null customer name can instead mean a missing name.

items.says: Add the period covered by the data-quality checks and explain what counted as a broken load.
items.because: That would make the figure of 15 more meaningful.

items.says: Clarify your role in developing the recommendations.
Avoid implying that presenting the recommendations caused their funding without support.
items.because: The connection is not established by the bullet.

items.says: Do not imply that the funded recommendations were implemented.
items.because: Funding does not necessarily mean implementation.

items.says: A simple average of regional rates is not generally the national conversion rate.
items.because: Regions can have different traffic volumes, so the overall rate must use combined totals.

items.says: Clarify the repeat-purchase measurement period, cohort definition, and your contribution.
Do not claim the dashboard caused the repeat-purchase increase without support.
items.because: Marketing’s use of it for retargeting alone does not establish causation.

items.says: Distinguish the five-percentage-point change from a relative percentage increase.
Define the basis for the 12% mean absolute error.
items.because: Mean absolute error is ordinarily in the predicted demand’s units, so a percentage needs a clear normalization.

items.says: Explain the training and test split and how future information was excluded.
Make the simulation context prominent and clarify what was replayed.
items.because: The result comes from a replay, not a live operational deployment.

items.says: Explain the comparison’s assumptions and whether the reduction came from the forecast-driven approach.
items.because: A different schedule or other assumptions could account for the result.

items.says: Do not imply that the city endorsed or adopted the work.
items.because: A link from the open-data team’s page shows only that the work was linked.

items.says: Include a working link to the published work in the actual résumé if appropriate.
Clarify your role in the three-person team and who made the shift change.
items.because: The bullet jumps from analysis to an operational result without showing who made the change.

items.says: Explain how the Saturday line-time comparison was measured and attributed.
items.because: The bullet does not show how the result was attributed.

items.says: Clarify your role and how repeat visitors were matched.
items.because: Matching handwritten records can be uncertain.

items.says: Ensure the visit-record work was authorized and public materials expose no confidential information.
items.because: The visit records are sensitive.

items.says: Remove the 2.4-million-shopper retention-dashboard bullet from the pantry project.
items.because: It appears copied from the Brightcart role, is unrelated to a food pantry, and undermines credibility.

items.says: Give more detail about the tools behind the dashboards or analysis.
items.because: The résumé currently gives no detail about that environment.

items.says: Keep “metric design” only if you can demonstrate sound definitions and aggregation choices.
items.because: The national conversion-rate calculation is incorrect.
